scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) just time out.
The partner operator reports the reverse direction fails too, but
differently: pings from pc2 toward 195.11.14.x die immediately
with "Destination Net Unreachable" from their own gateway
200.1.1.1. Both sides confirm the eBGP session between router1
and router2 shows Established. Diagnose.

injection.action: remove the network advertisement for pc1's subnet from router1's BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 BGP configuration (network statement)
Mechanism: router1's `router bgp 1` section no longer contains
  `network 195.11.14.0/24`, so router1 sends router2 an UPDATE
  withdrawing that prefix. The eBGP session itself stays
  Established and router1 still learns 200.1.1.0/24, so the
  FORWARD path pc1 -> router1 -> router2 -> pc2 still delivers.
  The RETURN path is dead: router2 has no route to 195.11.14.0/24,
  so pc2's replies (and pc2-originated pings toward pc1) are
  rejected at router2 with ICMP net-unreachable, sourced from
  200.1.1.1, the router2 interface facing pc2. pc1 therefore sees
  pure timeouts while pc2 sees instant net-unreachable errors.
Localization: router1
Root cause: missing `network 195.11.14.0/24` advertisement in
  router1's BGP configuration
Fix: re-add the network statement on router1 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on router1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 1" -c "network 195.11.14.0/24"`
router2 re-learns 195.11.14.0/24 and two-way reachability returns.
(A `service frr restart` on router1 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: BGP export policy/origination on router1 for LAN 195.11.14.0/24.

Mechanism: Router1 learns 200.1.1.0/24 from router2 via eBGP and forwards pc1’s echo-requests toward pc2. However, router2 lacks any route to 195.11.14.0/24, so when pc2 replies, router2 immediately generates “Destination Net Unreachable” toward pc2. Thus pc1 sees silent timeouts (its requests arrive but replies can’t return), while pc2 sees immediate unreachables from its default gateway (200.1.1.1) when pinging 195.11.14.x.

Localization: Router2’s routing table has no entry for 195.11.14.0/24 (only connected 193.10.11.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24). BGP on router2 shows it receives 0 prefixes from router1 and sends 1. Conversely, router1’s BGP table shows it receives 1 prefix (200.1.1.0/24). Router1’s running-config has no address-family stanza nor “network 195.11.14.0/24” (nor redistribution), so it is not advertising its LAN to router2.

Root cause: Router1 is not originating/advertising 195.11.14.0/24 into BGP, leaving router2 without a route to pc1’s subnet.

Corrective fix: On router1, configure BGP to announce the LAN:
router bgp 1
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 195.11.14.0/24
(or selectively “redistribute connected” with a route-map). After applying, verify on router2 that it receives 195.11.14.0/24 (show bgp summary / show ip route), then re-test pings in both directions. This will restore symmetric reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly identifies router1 as the device failing to originate/advertise 195.11.14.0/24 and proposes fixes to router1's BGP configuration.
